newsitem.title: UK: UK banks launch principles on small business links.
newsitem.headline: UK banks launch principles on small business links.

text.p: British banks on Tuesday launched a Statement of Principles to govern their relationships with small businesses that get into financial difficulties.

The banks have been sensitive to the issue after they received a bad press during the last economic recession in the early 1990s when many small businesses went bust and banks were accused of not doing enough to help limit the damage.

The British Bankers' Association said the statement would lay out the key elements of best practise for both sides of the relationship emphasising the need to get the link right at the outset; the benefits of early advice; and early action when things start to go wrong.
Major banks have agreed to be bound by the statement from July 1 and will revise their systems and procedures to take the Principles into account.

"This is a real advance in showing business customers what they can expect from their banks and in return, what they can do to develop their relationship," said Tim Sweeney, director-general of the BBA.

Among the principles are undertakings by the banks to urge business customers to get independent advice before taking out a loan; that they will alert companies in writing when they spot problems; support meaningful rescue measures; and a pledge not to seek the immediate appointment of a receiver if the customer keeps to their side of the Principles.
Banks signing up for the statement cover over 95 percent of the market and include al four major UK clearing banks, the three main Scottish banks and major Irish banks.
